author: Matthew Neschis
title: Tampa Bay Rays pitcher pukes on the mound during his MLB season debut - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Neschis ,
1 hours ago Tampa Bay Rays hurler Jonathan Heasley was unable to stop himself from hurling on the mound — quite literally.
On Wednesday, Heasley’s first MLB appearance in two seasons swiftly went off the rails once the pitcher blew chunks on the field just three pitches into his outing versus the Baltimore Orioles . In a separate freak incident that occurred one day prior, Red Sox’s Masataka Yoshida was drilled by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle .
In the fifth inning of the Rays’ 11-2 loss, Heasley could be seen dry heaving and throwing up before raising his hands to signal for time. The 29-year-old barfed two additional times before a member of the training staff walked out to hand him a towel and cold water.

Upon being asked by Rays manager Kevin Cash if he was alright, Heasley appeared to reply “I’m good” while sporting a wide smile on his face.
Taking to social media, droves of viewers couldn’t help but poke fun at Heasley. “Needs to change his name to Hurley,” one X user wrote, with another adding: “He’s one heck of a hurler.”
A third chimed in, “Did anyone already say Tampa Bay ‘Sprays?’ I’ll show myself out.”
This surprisingly isn’t the first time that Heasley has dealt with an unexpected wave of nausea in the middle of a game. During the stoppage in play, Rays Baseball sideline reporter Ryan Bass said: “Heasley actually talked to this about us pregame when he arrived here.
“This is something he’s actually is regularly known for. He actually did hurl on the field when he was with [Triple-A] Durham.
“He said when he used to play high school football, it would happen regularly. He just has a weak stomach. It sometimes happens when his nerves kick up a little bit. He said, ‘I’m totally fine.'”
Back in August 2022, Heasley similarly vomited on the mound while starting for the Royals in a contest against the Arizona Diamondbacks. Speaking to reporters following the stomach-churning incident, the right-hander revealed he was more concerned about only pitching 4.2 innings.
“I feel good now. Most of you guys know this has happened before,” Heasley said at the time. “It happened last year in a game. I think it’s — I don’t know, honestly. There’s nothing I can do to stop it.
“It just kind of hits me sometimes. I think it’s a mix of adrenaline, everything, getting a little amped up, whatever. It sucks it happened when it did.
“I was more frustrated about not getting through that fifth inning. I knew the bullpen was a little thin today. I was more frustrated that I had to come out when I did and just kind of put the team in a tough spot.”
Upon getting back up on the rubber in Wednesday’s game, Heasley proceeded to surrender eight hits and five runs while striking out two hitters over four innings.
